answer_sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
        AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
        THEN net_amount
        ELSE 0
      END
    ),
    2
  ) AS net_revenue_q1_2024,
  COUNT(
    CASE
      WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN 1
    END
  ) AS lines_counted,
  COUNT(
    DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN order_key
    END
  ) AS orders_counted,
  MIN(
    CASE
      WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN order_date
    END
  ) AS first_day_covered,
  MAX(
    CASE
      WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN order_date
    END
  ) AS last_day_covered,
  ROUND(
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
        AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
        AND channel = 'physical'
        THEN net_amount
        ELSE 0
      END
    ),
    2
  ) AS net_physical,
  ROUND(
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
        AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
        AND channel = 'online'
        THEN net_amount
        ELSE 0
      END
    ),
    2
  ) AS net_online,
  ROUND(
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
        AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
        THEN gross_amount
        ELSE 0
      END
    ),
    2
  ) AS gross_same_window,
  ROUND(
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN delivery_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
        AND delivery_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
        THEN net_amount
        ELSE 0
      END
    ),
    2
  ) AS net_by_delivery_date
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line

body.value: One figure: 9,494,485.57 USD — what Contoso actually charged customers, after discount, on everything ordered during January, February and March 2024, across the whole business. It is `net_amount` summed over 11,452 order lines belonging to 4,816 orders, splitting 3,643,929.59 through the physical shops and 5,850,555.97 through the web shop (those two round to a cent under the total, each having been rounded separately). WHAT IT DOES NOT INCLUDE: no deduction for returns, refunds, allowances or taxes, because this bundle holds no such columns — discount is the only deduction that exists in it, and it came to 600,781.14, which is why the same quarter at list price is 10,095,266.71. Revenue is counted by when each order was PLACED, not delivered; on a delivery-date basis the same quarter is 9,632,138.35. No comparison to any other period, and no breakdown by product, region, brand or channel.

sections.title: Which declarations it read, and what each settled
sections.subtitle: the path the decision took through the ontology — read off the walk's own citations, never inferred from what it could have read

value: net_revenue.default.revenue_means_net binds `net_amount` and says a question saying revenue or sales is answered there and told it is NET, after discount; NetRevenue's own grounding declares `measure: net_amount`. The question's worry about returns and taxes does not arise in this bundle — it holds no returns, refunds, allowances or tax columns at all. The only thing taken out of gross here is discount (`discount_amount` is measured as exactly gross_amount - net_amount), so 'net' has exactly one available meaning and it is the one finance already labels Net Revenue.
'net revenue' = `net_amount` on v_contoso5_sales_line — what the customer was actually charged, i.e. gross less discount, summed in USD

store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel carries `applies: subject`, so its `default: physical` reaches only questions whose SUBJECT is a Store; the subject here is a measure. The rule states the operator's ruling of 2026-10-18 verbatim — 'correct is that both internet and physical shops combined make revenue' — and names 218,814,471.66 over both channels as the unqualified revenue figure, not 132,024,417.53. This matches the question's own reading of 'the whole business, everything combined'.
'the net revenue (whole business)' = both sales channels — the physical shops and the web shop together, no channel predicate

v_contoso5_sales_line.currency_code is declared THE CURRENCY TRANSACTED IN and NOT the unit of the amounts; currency.ambiguity.code_is_not_the_unit_of_the_amounts forbids treating the USD amounts as if they were in that currency. No conversion applied, and none should be.
'amounts are USD' = the figures are already USD on every line and need no FX conversion

Nothing in this bundle declares a fiscal calendar — there is no fiscal-year column, no period table and no rule naming a fiscal offset anywhere in the concepts, relations or edges. The calendar reading is the only one the data can express, so this is not a choice I am making over an alternative, it is the absence of an alternative.
'Q1 2024' = the calendar quarter, 1 January to 31 March 2024 inclusive

order.default.period_is_order_date binds both columns with `default: ordered` and states the reason the choice matters: both dates are on every line and they differ, so the choice moves revenue between periods without changing the ten-year total — invisible in any one figure. Order date is declared the reporting convention; delivery is a logistics question. v_contoso5_sales_line.order_date additionally carries `period_binding: True`, so the quarter grain is computed on it.
'in Q1 2024' = by `order_date` — the day the order was placed

order.resolution.the_anchor_is_the_newest_order governs only periods named RELATIVE to now (this quarter, latest, year to date). Q1 2024 is absolute, so no anchoring is needed and the ten-month gap between the newest order (2025-12-31) and today's date does not bear on this answer.
'during' = a fixed, absolute window named by the question

net_revenue.default.revenue_means_net binds `net_amount` and instructs: answer there and SAY NET, the pre-discount figure being GrossRevenue; NetRevenue's grounding declares `measure: net_amount`. The question's worry about returns and taxes cannot arise — there are no returns, refunds, allowances or tax columns in this bundle, and `discount_amount` is measured as exactly gross_amount - net_amount, so discount is the only thing 'net' can be net OF. The reading 'whatever finance already labels net revenue' IS this column: it surfaces as 'net revenue' and its concept is labelled Net Revenue.
'net revenue' = `net_amount` summed — list value less discount, what the customer was actually charged: 9,494,485.57

order.default.period_is_order_date, `default: ordered`, with its reason stated: both dates are on every line and differ, so this choice shifts revenue between periods without changing the ten-year total — invisible in any single figure. Order date is the declared reporting convention; delivery is a logistics question. A declaration settles it so I did not ask, but the reader should know the quarter is 137,652.78 larger on a delivery basis, and that the gap is only which side of 1 January and 1 April a few days' shipping lands on — not extra trade.
'in Q1 2024' = by `order_date`, when the order was placed: 9,494,485.57

Not a live fork and not priceable: there is no fiscal-year column, no period or calendar relation, and no rule naming a fiscal offset in any declared concept, relation or edge. The calendar reading is the only one this bundle can express.
'Q1 2024 (calendar or fiscal)' = the calendar quarter, 1 January – 31 March 2024

store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel carries `applies: subject`, scoping its `default: physical` to questions whose subject is a Store; the subject here is a measure. The rule records the operator's ruling of 2026-10-18 verbatim — 'correct is that both internet and physical shops combined make revenue' — and the `channel` column states the same: a financial question naming no channel covers both. This agrees with the question's own reading, 'the whole business, everything combined'. Note that in this quarter the web shop outsells the shops, so silently excluding it would have been the single largest error available here.
'the net revenue (whole business)' = both channels together — physical shops and the web shop: 9,494,485.57

currency_code is declared the currency TRANSACTED IN and expressly not the unit of the amounts; currency.ambiguity.code_is_not_the_unit_of_the_amounts forbids presenting USD amounts as if they were in a filtered currency, and the order__converts_at__exchange_rate edge warns that nothing should multiply net_amount by a rate to obtain USD. The question named no currency, so no conversion arises.
'amounts are USD' = already USD on every line; no FX conversion applied

value.means: One figure: 9,494,485.57 USD — what Contoso actually charged customers, after discount, on everything ordered during January, February and March 2024, across the whole business. It is `net_amount` summed over 11,452 order lines belonging to 4,816 orders, splitting 3,643,929.59 through the physical shops and 5,850,555.97 through the web shop (those two round to a cent under the total, each having been rounded separately). WHAT IT DOES NOT INCLUDE: no deduction for returns, refunds, allowances or taxes, because this bundle holds no such columns — discount is the only deduction that exists in it, and it came to 600,781.14, which is why the same quarter at list price is 10,095,266.71. Revenue is counted by when each order was PLACED, not delivered; on a delivery-date basis the same quarter is 9,632,138.35. No comparison to any other period, and no breakdown by product, region, brand or channel.

readings.declaration: net_revenue.default.revenue_means_net binds `net_amount` and instructs: answer there and SAY NET, the pre-discount figure being GrossRevenue; NetRevenue's grounding declares `measure: net_amount`. The question's worry about returns and taxes cannot arise — there are no returns, refunds, allowances or tax columns in this bundle, and `discount_amount` is measured as exactly gross_amount - net_amount, so discount is the only thing 'net' can be net OF. The reading 'whatever finance already labels net revenue' IS this column: it surfaces as 'net revenue' and its concept is labelled Net Revenue.

readings.took: by `order_date`, when the order was placed: 9,494,485.57
readings.could_also_mean: by `delivery_date`, when it arrived: 9,632,138.35 — 137,652.78 higher, 1.45% of the figure
readings.declaration: order.default.period_is_order_date, `default: ordered`, with its reason stated: both dates are on every line and differ, so this choice shifts revenue between periods without changing the ten-year total — invisible in any single figure. Order date is the declared reporting convention; delivery is a logistics question. A declaration settles it so I did not ask, but the reader should know the quarter is 137,652.78 larger on a delivery basis, and that the gap is only which side of 1 January and 1 April a few days' shipping lands on — not extra trade.

readings.declaration: Not a live fork and not priceable: there is no fiscal-year column, no period or calendar relation, and no rule naming a fiscal offset in any declared concept, relation or edge. The calendar reading is the only one this bundle can express.

readings.took: both channels together — physical shops and the web shop: 9,494,485.57
readings.could_also_mean: physical shops only, 3,643,929.59, dropping the web shop's 5,850,555.97 — which in this quarter is 62% of the money, the larger half
readings.declaration: store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel carries `applies: subject`, scoping its `default: physical` to questions whose subject is a Store; the subject here is a measure. The rule records the operator's ruling of 2026-10-18 verbatim — 'correct is that both internet and physical shops combined make revenue' — and the `channel` column states the same: a financial question naming no channel covers both. This agrees with the question's own reading, 'the whole business, everything combined'. Note that in this quarter the web shop outsells the shops, so silently excluding it would have been the single largest error available here.

readings.took: already USD on every line; no FX conversion applied

readings.declaration: currency_code is declared the currency TRANSACTED IN and expressly not the unit of the amounts; currency.ambiguity.code_is_not_the_unit_of_the_amounts forbids presenting USD amounts as if they were in a filtered currency, and the order__converts_at__exchange_rate edge warns that nothing should multiply net_amount by a rate to obtain USD. The question named no currency, so no conversion arises.
